parts.label: (a)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Equate the expressions and multiply each term by $x^{1/2}$: $2x-12x^{1/2}+10=0$, or $x-6x^{1/2}+5=0$ — *M1. OE. Coefficients need to be retained but condone sign errors. Allow $x^{1/2}$ replaced by a substitution.
$(x^{1/2}-1)(x^{1/2}-5)=0$, or solve their three-term quadratic — DM1. OE.
$x=1$ and $x=25$ — A1.
$y=15$ and $y=13$ respectively — A1. If M1DM0 scored, SCB1B1 is available for final answers. Answers without working score 0/4.
Total: 4

parts.label: (b)
parts.official_mark_scheme_text:
Area $=\int[(3x^{-1/2}+12)-(2x^{1/2}+13x^{-1/2})]dx$ $[=\int(-2x^{1/2}+12-10x^{-1/2})dx]$ — M1. Attempt to integrate, defined by at least one correct fractional power, and subtract; condone wrong way round.
Antiderivative $=-\frac{2x^{3/2}}{3/2}+12x-\frac{10x^{1/2}}{1/2}$ — B1 B1. B1 for either braced fractional-power term; B1 for completely correct integration following sign errors from subtraction.
$\left(-\frac43(\text{their }25)^{3/2}+12(\text{their }25)-20(\text{their }25)^{1/2}\right)-\left(-\frac43(\text{their }1)^{3/2}+12(\text{their }1)-20(\text{their }1)^{1/2}\right)$ — M1. OE. Substitute their positive limits from (a) in their integrated expression and subtract; defined by at least one correct fractional power.
Alternative: $\int(3x^{-1/2}+12)dx-\int(2x^{1/2}+13x^{-1/2})dx$ — M1. Same integration-attempt guidance.
Alternative antiderivatives: $\frac{3x^{1/2}}{1/2}+12x$ minus $\frac{2x^{3/2}}{3/2}+\frac{13x^{1/2}}{1/2}$ — B1 B1. One mark for each correct integrated expression.
Alternative limits: $[(6(\text{their }25)^{1/2}+12(\text{their }25))-(6(\text{their }1)^{1/2}+12(\text{their }1))]-[(\frac43(\text{their }25)^{3/2}+26(\text{their }25)^{1/2})-(\frac43(\text{their }1)^{3/2}+26(\text{their }1)^{1/2})]$ — M1. OE. Both integrated expressions must use their positive limits and be subtracted.
Area $=\frac{128}{3}$ or $42.7$ AWRT — A1. If M1B1B1M0 then SC B1 available for correct final answer. Condone negative answer if corrected. Condone presence of $\pi$ for first four marks, but use of $\int 2y$ scores 0/5.
Total: 5
